observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a used engine assembly with plastic cover text reading 'FSI TURBO'.
A barcode/VIN-style sticker is visible on the engine cover in photo 1 but the printed numbers are too small/blurry to read.
Photo 2 shows alternator, A/C compressor, and hoses on the same engine from another angle; general wear and surface dirt visible, no visible cracks or fluid leaks in the frame.
Background in photos 0 and 1 shows a busy used-parts market (stacked engines, workers, tarps), consistent with a 'tokunbo' spare-parts yard in Abuja.
Watermark 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' is a seller/shop name overlay, not a brand marking on the engine itself.
No ignition test, compression test, or start-up video/photo is shown; engine is static and out of a vehicle.

identity.kind: used car engine (FSI Turbo type, make/model not confirmed)

claims.claim: Also deals on all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business claim, not shown or contradicted by the photos of this single engine.

risks.risk: Exact engine code/displacement (e.g. 1.8T FSI vs 2.0T FSI) cannot be confirmed, which materially changes compatibility and value.
risks.proof: Close-up clear photo of the VIN/engine code sticker seen in photo 1, or the stamped code on the block.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified/generic FSI turbo pull, at the lower end of that family

risks.risk: Running condition unknown; engine could be non-functional, have internal damage, or be sold 'as-is' without testing.
risks.proof: Video of the engine being started and idling, or a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Mileage or accident/flood history cannot be judged from static photos.
risks.proof: Odometer photo from donor vehicle or a mileage/history document.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown history, no premium for low mileage

risks.risk: Completeness of ancillaries (sensors, wiring harness, turbo unit itself) not fully confirmed across all three photos.
risks.proof: Full 360° photo set showing turbo, intake, and harness connectors intact.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly incomplete, missing-parts assumption

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine code/VIN sticker shown in photo 1.
Video of the engine running or at least turning over.
Photo of the donor vehicle's odometer or any paperwork showing mileage.
Full set of photos showing turbo unit and wiring harness completeness.
response.reason: The engine is visibly an FSI Turbo type but the exact code/displacement sticker is unreadable, and this detail drives compatibility and price tier in the spare-parts market, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without it.
